pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/headless.rs:72 fleet close/hibernate is a single-pid forcible kill (PTY lane the same via pty.rs:649 clone_killer; commands.rs:251 goes straight to killer.kill(), no polite rung) and never the tree, though src-tauri/src/webbuild/devserver.rs:595 kill_tree exists - a closed claude session leaves its MCP servers and tool shells as unowned orphans

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/headless.rs:72 PidKiller kills one pid with no polite rung and no descendant/tree kill; src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/commands.rs:251 documents hard-kill-first as the only path

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/registry.rs:667 is_live_state defines what occupies a live slot against the configured cap (stale.rs:167 live_slot_cap); queue.rs:1619 promote_head admits queued sessions as slots free
src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs:424 track_silence keys silence per session id, and the stale/stalled cutoffs degrade the claim (stale.rs:187) rather than kill

techniques.technique: session-reuse (invalidate-on-failure, idle expiry, one hash helper)
techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/execution.rs:2487 offers only when result.success; session_pool.rs:74 TTL expiry; session_pool.rs:81 exact-match retire; both sides call compute_config_hash (executions.rs:585)

pairs.registryProposal: session-reuse could name the explicit-invalidation-door gap: this repo invalidates via edit-command call sites (personas.rs, use_cases.rs, persona_brain.rs) as well as the fingerprint, and the sites that forgot (tool assign/unassign, credential edit) are exactly where the fingerprint is also blind - two mechanisms that each cover part of the inputs, with no check that their union is complete.
